Let $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ be an instance of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$-{\sc Retraction}.
We build an instance~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ of {\sc Surjective $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$-Colouring}
in the following fashion. First, take a copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ together with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ and build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ by identifying these on the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ that they both possess as a subgraph.
Let $m$ be the size of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ and consider its Hamilton cycle $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0$. We build $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$ by augmenting a new copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ for every vertex
$v \in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}') \setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$. 
Vertex~$v$ is to be identified with any vertex in the top copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}^*_m}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ and the bottom copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}^*_m}$ is to be identified with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ according to the identity function.
See Figure~\ref{f-new} for an example.
We claim that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ if and only if there exists a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$  to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$.

First suppose that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$.
Let $h$ be a retraction from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$. We extend $h$ as follows. First we map the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to itself in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ by the identity. This will ensure surjectivity. We then map the various copies of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$. This is always possible: because $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ retracts to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$, we have $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0])=V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$ due to Lemma~\ref{lem:spillage}. Hence, if $h(x)=y$ for two vertices $x\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}')\setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ and $y\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$, we can always find a retraction of the graph $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ that maps $x$ to $y$, and we mimic this retraction on the corresponding subgraph in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$. The crucial observation is that this can be done independently for each vertex in $V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}')\setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$, as two vertices of different copies of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ are only adjacent if they both belong to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'$.
This leads to a surjective homomorphism from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$.

Now suppose that there exists a surjective homomorphism~$h$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$  to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$.
If $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=1$, then by Lemma~\ref{lem:claim1}, $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m})|=1$ for all copies of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}''$. This means that $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'')|=1$ and $h$ is not surjective, a contradiction. Now, $1<|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|<m$ is not possible either due to Lemma~\ref{lem:under-m}. Thus, $|h(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)|=m$ and indeed $h$ maps $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ to a copy of itself in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ which we will call $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0=i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$ for some isomorphism~$i$. 

We claim that $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$. In order to see this, consider a vertex $y\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$. 
As $h$ is surjective, there exists a vertex~$x\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}'')$ with $h(x)=y$. By construction, $x$ belongs to some copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}^*_m}$, and thus also belongs to some copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}^*_m}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)$.
We can extend $i^{-1}$ to an isomorphism from the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$  (which has $i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)$ as its bottom cycle)  in the graph $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0',i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0))$ to the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ (which has $\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0$ as its bottom cycle) in the graph $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)$.

We observe that $r^*(u)=u$ if $u\in V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0')$ as $h$ coincides with $i$ on $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$. As $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ separates the other vertices of 
the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{Cyl}^*_m}$ from $V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})\setminus V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0)$, in the sense that removing $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$ would disconnect them, this means that $r^*$ is a retraction from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0',i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0))$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$. We find that $r^*$ maps $i(x)$ to $h\circ i^{-1}(i(x))=h(x)=y$. Moreover, as $x$ is in some copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}^*_m}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0,\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)$, we have that $i(x)$ is in some copy of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{DC}^*_m}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{F}}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0))$. We may assume without loss of generality that $i(x)$ belongs to the top copy (cf. Remark~1). We conclude that $y$ always belongs to  $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)])$ (cf. Remark~1).

As $\mathrm{Spill}_m(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}[\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0,i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{HC}}_0)]) = V(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$, we find, by assumption of the lemma, that there exists a retraction $r$ from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$ to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}'_0$.  
Now $i^{-1} \circ r \circ h$ ia the desired retraction of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{G}}$ to~$\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}_0$.

\noindent {\em Proof of Claim 0}: let $f$ be an endomorphism of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}}$. Then $f$ maps loops to loops. Since $(1,2)\in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$, $f$ can either map both to 1, both to 2 , or fix both. Clearly if it fixes both $f$ is the identity. Otherwise, if $f(1)=f(2)=i$, then $(f(0),i) , (i,f(0)) \in E(\ensuremath{\mathrm{H}})$ so $f(0)=i$. 

Without fear of confusion, we denote the constant maps by 0, 1 and 2. We denote the identity map by $id$.
